Researchers conduct two separate randomized controlled trials to assess the effect of a new antihypertensive drug.
In Study A, 100 participants are enrolled, and the standard deviation of systolic blood pressure reduction is 20 mmHg.
In Study B, 400 participants are enrolled, and the standard deviation of systolic blood pressure reduction is 20 mmHg.
Both studies find a mean reduction in systolic blood pressure of 10 mmHg.
The researchers use a 95% confidence interval for the mean reduction in systolic blood pressure.
